132:{"timestamp":"2026-08-22T07:00:56.499Z","ordinal":131,"type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"item_completed","thread_id":"01a0283e-c238-7442-8966-c1e348f270a1","turn_id":"01a0283f-46a0-7400-9217-ad62b2d8671f","item":{"type":"McpToolCall","id":"exec-db39511e-38cc-458b-b835-211e5a41de31","server":"linear","tool":"get_document","arguments":{"id":"d73de613-259a-4dde-9ad2-8fe785f4b39c"},"readOnlyHint":true,"status":"completed","result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{"id":"d73de613-259a-4dde-9ad2-8fe785f4b39c","title":"Architecture & Delivery Plan — SKI-12: Support Git-hosted skill sources and repository-wide imports","content":"Backlog issue: [SKI-12](<https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-12/support-git-hosted-skill-sources-and-repository-wide-imports>)\n\n## Status\n\nThis is a proposed architecture based on the requested behavior and Skillplane's known immutable-version model. Exact repository services, database schema, provider abstractions, deployment topology, and UI code must be inspected before implementation.\n\n## Current-state constraints\n\n* Skillplane manages immutable skill bundles and published/candidate versions.\n* Existing amendment policy controls review or trusted publication.\n* Tenancy, visibility, authorization, audit, and contexts must remain authoritative.\n* A mutable Git branch cannot replace immutable Skillplane version identity.\n* Exact current Git integration capabilities are **not yet defined**.\n\n## Proposed component model\n\n### Git source registry\n\nA workspace-scoped source record representing a repository and connection policy.\n\nProposed fields:\n\n* source ID and workspace ID;\n* canonical provider/repository identity and display URL;\n* default ref strategy: pinned commit, tracked branch, or tracked tag;\n* credential connection reference for private access, never a raw secret;\n* discovery mode and optional manifest path;\n* sync policy and current status;\n* created/updated/archived timestamps and actor attribution.\n\n### Skill source binding\n\nConnects one managed skill to one path in a source.\n\nProposed fields:\n\n* source ID and skill ID;\n* repository-relative skill root or `SKILL.md` path;\n* optional per-binding ref override;\n* discovery key or upstream identity;\n* last successful commit and content digest;\n* drift/action state;\n* unique constraints preventing ambiguous duplicate bindings.\n\n### Sync run and per-binding result\n\nRecords one immutable synchronization attempt:\n\n* requested ref and resolved commit SHA;\n* trigger and actor;\n* start/end timestamps;\n* repository tree digest where useful;\n* per-skill added/changed/unchanged/missing/conflict/error outcomes;\n* candidate/version IDs created;\n* sanitized provider diagnostics.\n\n### Version provenance\n\nEvery source-created candidate/version should retain:\n\n* source ID;\n* repository identity and URL;\n* resolved commit SHA;\n* source path;\n* source content/bundle digest;\n* sync run ID;\n* import actor and policy outcome.\n\n## Synchronization pipeline\n\n 1. Authorize the actor for the workspace and source.\n 2. Resolve repository connection and credential reference.\n 3. Resolve the requested branch/tag/commit to an exact commit SHA.\n 4. Fetch a bounded tree or required paths through a constrained provider adapter.\n 5. Discover skill roots deterministically.\n 6. Validate paths, file types, sizes, manifests, bundle limits, and metadata.\n 7. Build the canonical Skillplane file set without executing repository code.\n 8. Compare source digests with current bindings and managed versions.\n 9. Produce a preview: add, update, unchanged, missing, renamed candidate, or conflict.\n10. On confirmed apply, create/import through existing immutable version and amendment-policy services.\n11. Persist sync results and provenance transactionally where possible.\n12. Read back created candidates/versions and update source health.\n\nA no-op comparison must not create a new version.\n\n## Single-file mode\n\n* User supplies source, ref policy, and one `SKILL.md` or skill-root path.\n* Validation confirms the path belongs to the resolved repository tree.\n* The binding maps exactly one managed skill to that path.\n* The Diffpanel example uses repository-relative path `skills/diffpanel-chapters/SKILL.md`; the canonical repository URL remains to be supplied.\n\n## Repository-wide mode\n\n**Proposal:** support a deterministic discovery precedence:\n\n1. explicit repository manifest, if defined;\n2. recognized skill metadata files;\n3. bounded recursive discovery of `SKILL.md` roots.\n\nThe final convention is **not yet defined**. Discovery must preview every candidate and flag duplicate slugs, nested roots, unsupported bundles, and conflicting existing bindings.\n\nOne source detail endpoint/view returns all bindings with path, managed skill, resolved commit, digest, sync result, and drift state.\n\n## Provider abstraction\n\nDefine a narrow interface for:\n\n* canonicalize repository identity;\n* verify access;\n* resolve ref to commit;\n* list bounded tree;\n* fetch bounded blobs;\n* register/verify webhooks if supported;\n* expose rate-limit and retry metadata.\n\nInitial provider selection is open. Public GitHub is a likely first candidate because the supplied collection example is GitHub-hosted, but this is a proposal, not a confirmed requirement.\n\n## Security and supply-chain controls\n\n* Never execute hooks, package scripts, binaries, or repository code.\n* Reject absolute paths, traversal, symlink escape, unsafe submodules, unsupported media, and decompression bombs.\n* Bound file count, per-file bytes, expanded bundle bytes, repository traversal depth, and total sync work.\n* Treat manifests and Markdown as untrusted data.\n* Store private-repository authorization as scoped credential references with rotation and revocation.\n* Redact tokens and provider headers from logs and audit.\n* Verify webhook signatures, timestamps, replay IDs, installation identity, and repository binding.\n* Require workspace and skill authorization at both preview and apply.\n* Preserve existing visibility rules; a public repository does not automatically make a managed skill public.\n* Surface commit verification/signature information as evidence if available, without treating it as sufficient trust on its own.\n\n## Concurrency and idempotency\n\n* Key sync application by source, resolved commit, discovery configuration, and content digest.\n* Use per-source serialization or optimistic concurrency to avoid racing webhook/manual runs.\n* Make apply replay-safe after timeouts.\n* Do not recreate successful candidates or bindings when recovering partial runs.\n* For repository-wide sync, persist per-binding results so failed items can be retried without duplicating successful items.\n\n## Rename and deletion handling\n\n* Missing upstream paths mark bindings as action required; they do not archive or delete managed skills automatically.\n* Rename detection may use explicit upstream IDs, manifest keys, or digest similarity, but requires confirmation when ambiguous.\n* Source removal disconnects future synchronization while preserving immutable versions and provenance.\n* Force-push or unreachable historical commits must be visible; previously recorded provenance remains immutable.\n\n## API/MCP surface\n\n**Proposal:** paginated, authorization-filtered operations for:\n\n* create/get/list/update/archive/restore sources;\n* validate connection and preview discovery;\n* list source bindings and grouped skills;\n* create/update/remove a binding;\n* start/get/list sync runs;\n* preview and apply repository-wide changes;\n* filter skills by source and source status.\n\nExact tool/route names and least-privilege scopes are **not yet defined**. Long-running sync should use asynchronous jobs with status polling or events rather than holding a request open.\n\n## Reliability and observability\n\nTrack:\n\n* source access and auth failures;\n* ref resolution latency and errors;\n* provider rate limit and retry state;\n* discovered/changed/unchanged/conflicting counts;\n* no-op ratio;\n* candidate/publication outcomes;\n* webhook signature/replay failures;\n* sync duration, queue age, partial failures, and recovery;\n* drift age per binding.\n\nAlerting should distinguish provider outage, expired credentials, malformed repository content, policy rejection, and internal persistence failure.\n\n## Migration and compatibility\n\n* Add source records and optional bindings without changing existing skills.\n* Existing manual publish/amend flows remain authoritative and available.\n* A manually managed skill is connected only through an explicit, confirmed operation.\n* Define behavior for manual amendments to a source-bound skill before launch: reject, allow as divergence, or support overlays.\n* Rollback disables synchronization and webhooks while preserving source records, bindings, runs, versions, and provenance.\n\n## Delivery sequence\n\n### Phase 1: source and provenance contracts\n\n* Decide providers, ref policies, discovery convention, credential model, and manual-edit behavior.\n* Define schema, provider interface, provenance, API/MCP contracts, and limits.\n* Threat-model public and private source ingestion.\n\n### Phase 2: public single-file source\n\n* Implement public repository access, commit resolution, constrained file fetch, validation, preview, binding, and manual sync.\n* Integrate changed content with existing amendment policy.\n* Deliver source provenance on skill/version views.\n\n### Phase 3: repository-wide discovery\n\n* Add deterministic discovery and preview.\n* Add bulk binding/apply with per-item idempotency and recovery.\n* Deliver source detail and filter/group views.\n\n### Phase 4: private sources and automation\n\n* Add scoped credential connections and rotation.\n* Add webhook and/or scheduled synchronization after deciding trigger policy.\n* Add signature validation, replay protection, rate-limit handling, queues, and retries.\n\n### Phase 5: hardening and ecosystem integration\n\n* Load/performance tests for large repositories.\n* Rename/transfer/fork handling.\n* [skills.sh](<http://skills.sh>) integration only after its role and contract are defined.\n* Operational dashboards, alerts, and recovery tooling.\n\n## Validation\n\n* Unit tests for URL canonicalization, ref resolution, path validation, discovery, digesting, and provenance.\n* Contract tests against supported provider APIs.\n* Security tests for traversal, symlinks, submodules, oversized files, malicious manifests, secret redaction, and webhook replay.\n* Idempotency and concurrency tests for repeated/racing syncs.\n* Integration tests from repository commit to candidate/version and policy outcome.\n* Repository-wide partial-failure and recovery tests.\n* Cross-workspace and private-source authorization denial tests.\n* UI tests for source setup, preview, apply, source grouping, drift, and failure recovery.\n* Production canary with a controlled public repository before broader rollout.\n\n## Risks and mitigations\n\n* **Supply-chain compromise:** immutable commit provenance, review policy, no execution, and visible diffs.\n* **Credential leakage:** provider connections, least scopes, redaction, rotation, and audit.\n* **Mutable refs/force-pushes:** resolve every run to a commit and preserve prior provenance.\n* **Provider outages/rate limits:** queueing, backoff, status distinction, and manual retry.\n* **Mass unintended changes:** preview, bounded batches, policy gates, and non-destructive deletion handling.\n* **Layout ambiguity:** explicit manifest precedence and conflict states.\n* **State divergence:** define manual-edit/overlay behavior before source binding launch.\n\n## Open questions\n\nProvider scope, ref semantics, trigger modes, repository layout, overlay behavior, rename/deletion policy, source transfer identity, and [skills.sh](<http://skills.sh>) integration are blocking design decisions for later # Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images, videos, and audio using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When an app or connector generates or edits media at a remote URL and provides a user-facing preview or display tool, use that tool instead of embedding the URL in Markdown.
- When sending or referencing a local image, video, or audio file, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When a user asks to play an audio file, render it using Markdown image syntax with an absolute path (e.g., ![audio](/absolute/path.mp3)).
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Workspace Dependencies

A plugin is a local bundle of skills, MCP servers, and apps.
### How to use plugins
- Skill naming: If a plugin contributes skills, those skill entries are prefixed with `plugin_name:` in the Skills list.

# Skillplane OAuth interoperability diagnosis, backlog capture, and PostHog MCP analytics PR

Rollout context: Work occurred primarily in `/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/agent/experiments/skillplane`; later implementation used clean worktree `/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/agent/experiments/skillplane-posthog-pr` to avoid mutating the dirty `SKI-1` checkout.

## Task 1: Diagnose Claude MCP OAuth failure

Outcome: success

Preference signals:
- The user explicitly requested “read-only troubleshoot” and later “dont make any edits yet.. .just troubleshoot the root cuase” -> investigate code, live endpoints, standards, and production state without editing until separately authorized.

Key steps:
- Traced URL-form client resolution through `packages/authfn-mcp-oauth/src/clients.ts`, authorization handling, plugin routes, and error mapping.
- Fetched Claude’s live metadata at `https://claude.ai/oauth/mcp-oauth-client-metadata`; it returned valid JSON with exact `client_id`, redirect URI, public-client authentication, `response_types:["code"]`, and grants including `authorization_code`, `refresh_token`, and `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer`.
- Confirmed Skillplane rejects any advertised grant outside its closed allowlist at `clients.ts:152-159`, producing `invalid_client` with “The requested grant type is not supported.”
- Confirmed Claude’s actual authorization request uses authorization code plus PKCE S256; it is not requesting JWT bearer.
- Verified relevant MCP/OAuth specifications and historical Claude metadata. Archived metadata had only two grants on 2026-06-11 and added JWT bearer by 2026-07-29, exposing a latent implementation defect after the July 26 implementation.
- No files were changed.

Reusable knowledge:
- The bug is an abstraction error: `validateRegistration()` is shared by dynamic registration and Client ID Metadata Document hydration. Dynamic registration can reject unsupported grants, but a reusable client metadata document may advertise capabilities for other authorization servers.
- `grant_types_supported` describes what Skillplane issues; `grant_types` describes what the client may use. Metadata should accept additional registered grants while requiring a compatible authorization-code path for this request. The token endpoint can still reject an actual JWT-bearer token request with `unsupported_grant_type`.
- MCP’s main security requirements were implemented correctly: protected-resource and authorization-server discovery, URL client IDs, exact metadata identifier matching, exact redirects, resource/audience binding, PKCE S256, one-time codes, refresh rotation, and bearer-header-only handling.
- The conformance gap was testing only a hand-authored metadata document with exactly Skillplane’s grants and a wholly unsupported `["password"]` negative case; no test covered supported grants plus an extension grant.

Failures and how to do differently:
- Do not describe the original implementation as wholly non-standard; characterize it as mostly compliant but over-constrained and interoperability-incomplete.
- Do not claim the exact production exception without observability evidence. Earlier diagnostics were limited by Wrangler requiring Node 22 and unavailable Cloudflare observability access.

References:
- `packages/authfn-mcp-oauth/src/clients.ts:152-159, 218-262, 302-317`
- `packages/authfn-mcp-oauth/src/authorization.ts:89-138`
- Claude metadata: `https://claude.ai/oauth/mcp-oauth-client-metadata`
- MCP authorization spec: `https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/authorization`
- Historical metadata snapshots: 2026-06-11 had two grants; 2026-07-29 included JWT bearer.

## Task 1: Diagnose Claude MCP OAuth failure

Outcome: success

Preference signals:
- The user explicitly requested “read-only troubleshoot” and later “dont make any edits yet.. .just troubleshoot the root cuase” -> investigate code, live endpoints, standards, and production state without editing until separately authorized.

Key steps:

- Fetched Claude’s live metadata at `https://claude.ai/oauth/mcp-oauth-client-metadata`; it returned valid JSON with exact `client_id`, redirect URI, public-client authentication, `response_types:["code"]`, and grants including `authorization_code`, `refresh_token`, and `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer`.
- Confirmed Skillplane rejects any advertised grant outside its closed allowlist at `clients.ts:152-159`, producing `invalid_client` with “The requested grant type is not supported.”
- Confirmed Claude’s actual authorization request uses authorization code plus PKCE S256; it is not requesting JWT bearer.
- Verified relevant MCP/OAuth specifications and historical Claude metadata. Archived metadata had only two grants on 2026-06-11 and added JWT bearer by 2026-07-29, exposing a latent implementation defect after the July 26 implementation.
- No files were changed.

Reusable knowledge:
- The bug is an abstraction error: `validateRegistration()` is shared by dynamic registration and Client ID Metadata Document hydration. Dynamic registration can reject unsupported grants, but a reusable client metadata document may advertise capabilities for other authorization servers.
- `grant_types_supported` describes what Skillplane issues; `grant_types` describes what the client may use. Metadata should accept additional registered grants while requiring a compatible authorization-code path for this request. The token endpoint can still reject an actual JWT-bearer token request with `unsupported_grant_type`.
- MCP’s main security requirements were implemented correctly: protected-resource and authorization-server discovery, URL client IDs, exact metadata identifier matching, exact redirects, resource/audience binding, PKCE S256, one-time codes, refresh rotation, and bearer-header-only handling.
- The conformance gap was testing only a hand-authored metadata document with exactly Skillplane’s grants and a wholly unsupported `["password"]` negative case; no test covered supported grants plus an extension grant.

Failures and how to do differently:
- Do not describe the original implementation as wholly non-standard; characterize it as mostly compliant but over-constrained and interoperability-incomplete.
- Do not claim the exact production exception without observability evidence. Earlier diagnostics were limited by Wrangler requiring Node 22 and unavailable Cloudflare observability access.

  "instructions": "# Add to Backlog Workflow\n\nCapture the item being discussed in the current agent thread as a durable Linear backlog issue with two detailed supporting documents.\n\n## Required outcome\n\nProduce and verify:\n\n1. one issue in the relevant team's backlog;\n2. an Ideation and Product Rationale document linked to the issue;\n3. an Architecture and Delivery Plan document linked to the issue.\n\nTreat this as backlog capture, not authorization to implement, edit code, commit, push, deploy, assign people, or set dates.\n\n## 1. Synthesize the discussion\n\nRead the full relevant thread and distill the work item instead of copying the conversation verbatim.\n\nCapture:\n\n- problem or opportunity and user/business context;\n- desired outcome and success signals;\n- goals, non-goals, requirements, and constraints;\n- ideas, decisions, rejected alternatives, and tradeoffs;\n- architecture, interfaces, dependencies, data flow, and operational concerns discussed;\n- risks, unknowns, open questions, acceptance criteria, and next steps.\n\nSeparate facts from proposals. Label uncertain material as `Assumption`, `Proposal`, or `Open question`. Never invent decisions or technical details to make the backlog item look complete.\n\n## 2. Prepare the Linear payload\n\nPrepare a concise, outcome-oriented issue title and an initial description containing:\n\n- executive summary;\n- problem or opportunity;\n- expected outcome;\n- scoped goals and non-goals;\n- acceptance criteria;\n- dependencies and risks;\n- open questions.\n\nDo not include document links in the initial description because the documents do not exist yet.\n\nPrepare these required document specifications:\n\n### Ideation and Product Rationale\n\nTitle: `Ideation & Product Rationale — <ISSUE-ID>: <issue title>`\n\nInclude:\n\n- context and motivating problem;\n- target users or stakeholders;\n- use cases and user journeys;\n- ideas discussed;\n- desired outcomes and success measures;\n- alternatives, decisions, and rationale;\n- product, UX, and operational considerations;\n- assumptions, open questions, goals, non-goals, and acceptance criteria.\n\n### Architecture and Delivery Plan\n\nTitle: `Architecture & Delivery Plan — <ISSUE-ID>: <issue title>`\n\nInclude, when relevant:\n\n- current-state constraints;\n- proposed system or workflow architecture;\n- component boundaries and responsibilities;\n- data model, APIs, events, integrations, and data flow;\n- security, privacy, authorization, reliability, observability, migration, and rollback considerations;\n- dependencies, sequencing, implementation phases, validation, and rollout;\n- technical risks, tradeoffs, alternatives, assumptions, and open questions.\n\nFor non-software items, adapt architecture to the operating model, process, ownership, and information flow. State `Not yet defined` when the thread does not support a detail.\n\n## 3. Retrieve the shared Linear skill\n\nBefore any Linear mutation, retrieve and follow this exact published dependency through Skillplane:\n\n- workspace: `21n`\n- skill: `create-and-associate-linear-issue`\n- semantic version: `1.0.0`\n\nIf the exact dependency cannot be retrieved, stop before creating anything. Do not reconstruct it from memory or duplicate its routing, retry, association, recovery, or verification rules locally.\n\nProvide this handoff:\n\n```yaml\noperation: create_or_reuse\npurpose: backlog_capture\ndestinationHints: <project, team, repository, product, linked issue, and thread context>\ndesiredState: backlog\nissue:\n  title: <prepared title>\n  description: <prepared initial description without unresolved links>\nassociations:\n  - type: linear_document\n    required: true\n    title: Ideation & Product Rationale — <ISSUE-ID>: <issue title>\n    content: <prepared ideation document>\n  - type: linear_document\n    required: true\n    title: Architecture & Delivery Plan — <ISSUE-ID>: <issue title>\n    content: <prepared architecture document>\ncompletionRequirements:\n  - issue is in the resolved project and team\n  - actual state is Backlog or a disclosed fallback\n  - both documents exist and link back to the issue\n  - the issue links to both documents\n```\n\nUse the shared skill's returned issue identifier to finalize document titles and backlinks.\n\n## 4. Verify the result\n\nRequire the shared skill's read-back receipt. Confirm the issue identifier, direct URL, team, project, actual state, both document titles and URLs, bidirectional links, and absence of an unresolved partial-write marker.\n\nReport those results plus any state substitution, assumption, or unresolved destination field. Do not report completion until every required association and completion requirement passes.\n\n## Integrity rules\n\n- Keep issue and document content consistent and evidence-based.\n- Preserve the thread's intent without exposing secrets, tokens, private logs, customer-sensitive information, or unnecessary personal data.\n- Never guess a project or team.\n- If the shared skill cannot resolve a unique destination, ask the user before any Linear mutation.",

Provide the shared Linear mutation layer for parent skills and agent workflows. Resolve the correct destination, create or reuse one issue, associate required artifacts, recover partial writes, and verify the resulting Linear state.

## Handoff contract

Require the parent workflow to provide:

- `operation`: `create_or_reuse` or `associate_existing`;
- `purpose`: why the issue or association is needed;
- `destinationHints`: explicit project, team, repository, product, or existing Linear context;
- `desiredState`: semantic intent such as `backlog` or `active_development`;
- `issue`: title and evidence-based description when creating;
- `existingIssue`: issue identifier when associating with an existing issue;
- `associations`: required documents, commits, pull requests, deployments, or other references;
- `completionRequirements`: facts and links that must be verified before success.

Do not start Linear mutations when the handoff is missing information required to choose a unique destination or truthful state.

## 1. Resolve the destination

Use the Linear connector for every Linear read and write.

Resolve the project and team in this order:

1. project or team explicitly named by the user;
2. association already established in the current task or supplied issue;
3. repository or product ownership that maps to one Linear project and team.

Use the selected project's associated team. Never choose by name similarity alone. If the project is missing, spans multiple plausible teams, or conflicts with the handoff, ask the user before creating or moving anything.

## 2. Prevent duplicates and unsafe retries

- If `existingIssue` is supplied, retrieve it and verify its team, project, and state before associating anything.
- Before creating, search the resolved project and team for an equivalent active issue.
- If a likely duplicate exists, ask whether to reuse it or create a distinct issue; do not silently duplicate or merge work.
- After a timeout or ambiguous mutation response, read Linear state before retrying.
- Once an issue identifier is observed, preserve and reuse it for the rest of the workflow.

## 3. Create or reuse the issue

For `create_or_reuse`:

- Create one concise, outcome-oriented issue in the resolved team and attach it to the resolved project.
- Map `desiredState` to the team's truthful workflow state.
  - For `backlog`, use Backlog; if unavailable, use the nearest unstarted or triage state and disclose the substitution.
  - For `active_development`, use the team's active state such as In Progress.
- Do not invent priority, assignee, estimate, cycle, deadline, or completion state.
- Create the issue before documents or references that require its identifier.
- Do not place links in the initial description until their targets exist.

For `associate_existing`, do not create another issue.

Capture the issue identifier and direct URL.

## 4. Create and associate artifacts

Process associations in dependency order.

### Documents

- Create each required Linear document only after the issue identifier exists.
- Include the issue identifier and a backlink to the issue in every document.
- Associate each document with the issue using Linear's supported relationship or a visible issue link.
- After all documents exist, update the issue description or a clearly visible comment with their direct links.
- If Linear cannot create or associate the required documents, stop and report the capability limitation. Do not substitute local files or claim completion.

### Existing references

For commits, pull requests, deployments, or existing documents:

- Verify the supplied reference exists when the connector exposes that information.
- Link it to the existing issue without changing unrelated issue fields.
- Never invent a hash, URL, deployment result, or review state.

## 5. Recover partial writes

If the issue exists but an association fails:

- keep the same issue identifier;
- record or preserve an explicit `association incomplete` status in the issue when possible;
- retry only the missing association after checking current Linear state;
- do not recreate successful documents or duplicate issue comments;
- report the partial result and exact blocker if recovery cannot complete.

## 6. Verify and return a receipt

Read the issue and every required association back through Linear. Confirm:

- issue identifier and URL;
- team and project;
- actual workflow state and any disclosed substitution;
- issue title and essential description;
- every required association and backlink;
- no unresolved partial-write marker;
- every parent-supplied completion requirement.

Return a structured receipt containing those facts, plus assumptions, substitutions, and anything not verified. Do not report success until all blocking completion requirements pass.

## Integrity rules

- Preserve the parent workflow's authorization boundaries; this skill does not authorize implementation, commits, pushes, deployment, assignments, or dates.
- Keep issue content evidence-based and consistent with associated artifacts.
- Do not expose secrets, tokens, private logs, customer-sensitive information, or unnecessary personal data.
- Never fabricate destination mappings, issue identifiers, links, states, associations, or verification results.","files":[{"path":"SKILL.md","sha256":"afb81548531fed6c9bf61cb0fc73147d474df234a1ca7161bd208ff6d25bfc07","byteSize":5346,"mediaType":"text/markdown; charset=utf-8"},{"path":"skill.json","sha256":"a700b7fff27feda8388252b89ec18240ee3457d1bb8c52f2880ff7777244ad36","byteSize":705,"mediaType":"application/json"}],"context":null}},"duration":{"secs":0,"nanos":277212875}},"started_at_ms":1787381688794,"completed_at_ms":1787381689071}}

  "instructions": "# Create and Associate Linear Issue\n\nProvide the shared Linear mutation layer for parent skills and agent workflows. Resolve the correct destination, create or reuse one issue, associate required artifacts, recover partial writes, and verify the resulting Linear state.\n\n## Handoff contract\n\nRequire the parent workflow to provide:\n\n- `operation`: `create_or_reuse` or `associate_existing`;\n- `purpose`: why the issue or association is needed;\n- `destinationHints`: explicit project, team, repository, product, or existing Linear context;\n- `desiredState`: semantic intent such as `backlog` or `active_development`;\n- `issue`: title and evidence-based description when creating;\n- `existingIssue`: issue identifier when associating with an existing issue;\n- `associations`: required documents, commits, pull requests, deployments, or other references;\n- `completionRequirements`: facts and links that must be verified before success.\n\nDo not start Linear mutations when the handoff is missing information required to choose a unique destination or truthful state.\n\n## 1. Resolve the destination\n\nUse the Linear connector for every Linear read and write.\n\nResolve the project and team in this order:\n\n1. project or team explicitly named by the user;\n2. association already established in the current task or supplied issue;\n3. repository or product ownership that maps to one Linear project and team.\n\nUse the selected project's associated team. Never choose by name similarity alone. If the project is missing, spans multiple plausible teams, or conflicts with the handoff, ask the user before creating or moving anything.\n\n## 2. Prevent duplicates and unsafe retries\n\n- If `existingIssue` is supplied, retrieve it and verify its team, project, and state before associating anything.\n- Before creating, search the resolved project and team for an equivalent active issue.\n- If a likely duplicate exists, ask whether to reuse it or create a distinct issue; do not silently duplicate or merge work.\n- After a timeout or ambiguous mutation response, read Linear state before retrying.\n- Once an issue identifier is observed, preserve and reuse it for the rest of the workflow.\n\n## 3. Create or reuse the issue\n\nFor `create_or_reuse`:\n\n- Create one concise, outcome-oriented issue in the resolved team and attach it to the resolved project.\n- Map `desiredState` to the team's truthful workflow state.\n  - For `backlog`, use Backlog; if unavailable, use the nearest unstarted or triage state and disclose the substitution.\n  - For `active_development`, use the team's active state such as In Progress.\n- Do not invent priority, assignee, estimate, cycle, deadline, or completion state.\n- Create the issue before documents or references that require its identifier.\n- Do not place links in the initial description until their targets exist.\n\nFor `associate_existing`, do not create another issue.\n\nCapture the issue identifier and direct URL.\n\n## 4. Create and associate artifacts\n\nProcess associations in dependency order.\n\n### Documents\n\n- Create each required Linear document only after the issue identifier exists.\n- Include the issue identifier and a backlink to the issue in every document.\n- Associate each document with the issue using Linear's supported relationship or a visible issue link.\n- After all documents exist, update the issue description or a clearly visible comment with their direct links.\n- If Linear cannot create or associate the required documents, stop and report the capability limitation. Do not substitute local files or claim completion.\n\n### Existing references\n\nFor commits, pull requests, deployments, or existing documents:\n\n- Verify the supplied reference exists when the connector exposes that information.\n- Link it to the existing issue without changing unrelated issue fields.\n- Never invent a hash, URL, deployment result, or review state.\n\n## 5. Recover partial writes\n\nIf the issue exists but an association fails:\n\n- keep the same issue identifier;\n- record or preserve an explicit `association incomplete` status in the issue when possible;\n- retry only the missing association after checking current Linear state;\n- do not recreate successful documents or duplicate issue comments;\n- report the partial result and exact blocker if recovery cannot complete.\n\n## 6. Verify and return a receipt\n\nRead the issue and every required association back through Linear. Confirm:\n\n- issue identifier and URL;\n- team and project;\n- actual workflow state and any disclosed substitution;\n- issue title and essential description;\n- every required association and backlink;\n- no unresolved partial-write marker;\n- every parent-supplied completion requirement.\n\nReturn a structured receipt containing those facts, plus assumptions, substitutions, and anything not verified. Do not report success until all blocking completion requirements pass.\n\n## Integrity rules\n\n- Preserve the parent workflow's authorization boundaries; this skill does not authorize implementation, commits, pushes, deployment, assignments, or dates.\n- Keep issue content evidence-based and consistent with associated artifacts.\n- Do not expose secrets, tokens, private logs, customer-sensitive information, or unnecessary personal data.\n- Never fabricate destination mappings, issue identifiers, links, states, associations, or verification results.",

100:{"timestamp":"2026-08-22T06:56:35.109Z","ordinal":99,"type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"custom_tool_call","id":"ctc_0008af6bbe961572016a8947f8761487d0878c46f3f3f86ecb","status":"completed","call_id":"call_CjLV1ujPOwVmClV1TIEolp0I","name":"exec","input":"const groupDescription = `## Executive summary

Add workspace-level skill groups so Skillplane can organize related skills by domain and associate workspace members with those groups—for example Design, Marketing, Development, and Sales.

## Problem or opportunity

A flat workspace skill catalog does not express which skills belong together or which members should work with a domain-specific collection. As the catalog and workspace membership grow, discovery, onboarding, and administration become harder.

## Expected outcome

Workspace administrators can define reusable skill groups, associate skills and members with them, and inspect those relationships. Members can quickly find the skills relevant to their domains.

## Goals

- Create, rename, describe, archive, and restore skill groups within a workspace.
- Associate skills with skill groups.
- Associate workspace members with skill groups.
- Show and filter skills and members by group.
- Preserve workspace isolation, role-based administration, auditability, and deterministic API behavior.
- Define how group membership interacts with skill visibility and authorization before rollout.

## Non-goals

- Replacing existing workspace roles.
- Inferring a member's group from job title or behavior.
- Automatically generating or changing skill content.
- Implementing organization-wide groups shared across unrelated workspaces unless separately designed.

## Acceptance criteria

- A workspace can maintain domain groups such as Design, Marketing, Development, and Sales.
- Authorized administrators can add and remove skills and members without duplicate associations.
- Group detail views expose the associated skills and members; skill/member views expose their groups.
- Lists and search can filter by group.
- Archived groups do not silently delete skills, members, or historical audit records.
- Cross-workspace references are rejected.
- Every membership change is attributable in audit history.
- Existing workspaces continue to work without creating groups.
- Product and API semantics clearly state whether groups are organizational only or affect effective skill access.

## Dependencies and risks

- Existing workspace membership, skill visibility, authorization, and audit models.
- Risk of accidentally widening access if group membership is treated as a grant.
- Risk of confusing group membership with workspace role or team ownership.
- Migration and indexing requirements for existing skills and members.
- Large groups may require pagination and bulk-operation safeguards.

## Open questions

- Does membership grant skill access, configure defaults, or only categorize and filter?
- Can a skill and a member belong to multiple groups?
- Who may administer groups: owners only, or admins as well?
- Should personal workspaces support groups?
- How should group removal affect effective access, pinned skills, or agent configurations?
- Are nested groups needed, or should the first version remain flat?`;

const sourceDescription = `## Executive summary

Allow a Skillplane-managed skill to use a Git-hosted skill file as its source of truth, and allow one Git repository to act as a shared source for multiple skills. Expose source-level grouping so users can see every managed skill derived from a given repository or source configuration.

## Problem or opportunity

Skill authors already maintain canonical skill instructions in Git repositories. Copying those files into Skillplane creates drift, obscures provenance, and makes updates manual. Repository-scale collections such as [vercel-labs/skills](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) and catalogs surfaced through [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/) also need a single import and synchronization model rather than one disconnected setup per skill.

A concrete single-skill example is Diffpanel's repository file at \`skills/diffpanel-chapters/SKILL.md\`.

## Expected outcome

A workspace can register a Git source once, map one file to one managed skill or discover multiple skills from a repository, synchronize immutable Skillplane versions from exact Git revisions, and inspect all skills grouped by their common source.

## Goals

- Represent a Git source with repository identity, provider, ref policy, credentials where needed, and provenance.
- Configure an individual managed skill from one Git-hosted \`SKILL.md\` path.
- Import or synchronize multiple skills from a repository containing a skill collection.
- Track each published Skillplane version back to an exact commit and source path.
- Show and filter all skills associated with the same source.
- Detect changes, additions, removals, renames, failures, and drift without silently overwriting managed state.
- Support public repositories first while preserving a secure path for private repositories.

## Non-goals

- Executing arbitrary repository code during import.
- Treating a mutable branch name alone as immutable provenance.
- Automatically deleting managed skills when upstream files disappear.
- General-purpose Git hosting or repository mirroring.
- Assuming every repository follows one directory layout.

## Acceptance criteria

- A user can configure a single source using repository URL, ref policy, and \`SKILL.md\` path.
- A successful synchronization records the resolved commit SHA, source path, content digest, timestamp, and outcome.
- Repository-wide import discovers supported skills deterministically and previews changes before applying them.
- One source detail view lists every managed skill sourced from it, including sync and drift status.
- Repeated synchronization of the same commit and content is idempotent and does not create duplicate versions.
- Changed content creates a reviewable candidate or published version according to the skill's existing publication policy.
- Missing, renamed, malformed, or conflicting source files produce explicit non-destructive states.
- Repository content is treated as untrusted input: path traversal, symlink escape, oversized bundles, unsupported files, and secret exposure are prevented.
- Existing manually managed skills remain unchanged until explicitly connected to a source.
- Source removal does not erase immutable Skillplane version history.

## Dependencies and risks

- Existing immutable bundle/version, amendment review, visibility, tenancy, audit, and credential models.
- Git provider API limits, webhook reliability, force-pushes, deleted refs, and private repository authorization.
- Repository discovery conventions and conflicts between source metadata and Skillplane metadata.
- Supply-chain risks from compromised repositories or mutable refs.
- Scale limits for large monorepos and bulk synchronization.

## Open questions

- Which providers and URL forms are supported first?
- Are refs pinned to commits, tracked branches/tags, or both?
- Is synchronization manual, scheduled, webhook-driven, or configurable?
- What repository layouts and manifests define multiple skills?
- How are upstream rename and deletion intents confirmed?
- Can one managed skill combine Git-sourced files with Skillplane-managed overlays?
- How are forks and repository transfers represented without losing provenance?
- Should skills.sh be integrated as a catalog/discovery layer, a Git source resolver, or both?`;

const groupIdeation = `# Ideation & Product Rationale — ${gIssue}: Support skill groups and workspace member assignments

Backlog issue: [${gIssue}](${gUrl})

## Context and motivating problem

Skillplane currently presents a workspace's skills without a domain grouping layer. A flat catalog becomes harder to navigate and administer as the number of skills and members grows. The requested capability is to group skills into areas such as Design, Marketing, Development, and Sales, then associate workspace members with the relevant groups.

This document captures product intent. It does not authorize implementation, staffing, or dates.

## Target users and stakeholders

- Workspace owners and administrators who organize skills and membership.
- Workspace members who need a focused view of domain-relevant skills.
- Skill authors and maintainers who need discoverability without duplicating skills.
- Security and operations stakeholders responsible for authorization and auditability.
- Agent clients that may eventually consume group-aware skill discovery through APIs or MCP.

## Core use cases

### Organize a domain catalog

An administrator creates a “Design” group, adds design-related skills, and sees the group as one coherent collection.

### Onboard a workspace member

An administrator associates a new designer with the Design group. The member can discover the skills relevant to that domain without searching the full catalog.

### Support cross-functional work

A member or skill may need to appear in more than one domain, such as Design and Marketing.

**Proposal:** model both relationships as many-to-many. This is not yet a confirmed decision.

### Audit and maintain groups

An administrator can inspect membership, understand who changed it, archive an obsolete group, and preserve historical evidence without deleting the underlying skills or members.

## Product principles

- Groups are workspace-scoped and cannot reference another workspace's records.
- Groups complement workspace roles; they do not replace owner, admin, editor, or viewer semantics.
- Membership is explicit. Skillplane should not infer it from titles, activity, or private data.
- Archive is preferred over destructive deletion when relationships or audit history exist.
- Existing workspaces remain valid with zero groups.

## Ideas discussed and product options

### Option A: organizational grouping only

Groups drive labels, navigation, filtering, and onboarding but do not change authorization.

- Lower security risk and simpler initial delivery.
- Does not solve cases where group membership is intended to grant access.

### Option B: group-based skill availability

A member's groups determine which workspace skills are available to them.

- Stronger delegation and least-privilege potential.
- Creates a new authorization layer and requires careful precedence rules.

### Option C: separate organization and access controls

A group organizes skills and members, while an explicit policy flag or separate access policy determines whether it grants availability.

- More expressive and safer long term.
- Higher conceptual and implementation complexity.

**Open question:** which option reflects the intended first release? The request supports organization and member association, but does not establish access-control semantics.

## Desired outcomes and success measures

- Administrators can create domain groups and maintain skill/member associations without duplicates.
- Members find relevant skills with fewer catalog searches.
- Group filters and detail views return consistent results across UI and API surfaces.
- No group operation leaks or links cross-workspace records.
- Group archival and membership changes remain auditable.
- Existing workspaces and skills require no migration action to continue working.
- If groups affect authorization, permission tests show no accidental access widening.

Potential quantitative measures are not yet defined. Candidate measures include time to onboard a member, skill discovery success, percentage of skills organized, and failed/unauthorized group mutations.

## Product and UX considerations

- Group names should be clear within a workspace; uniqueness rules need definition.
- Group cards or rows should show skill and member counts.
- Skill and member detail views should expose group membership.
- Filtering should support one or multiple groups if many-to-many is adopted.
- Empty groups should be valid during setup.
- Archived groups should disappear from normal selection while remaining recoverable.
- Bulk assignment may be important for large workspaces but should not obscure per-item failures.
- UI language must distinguish “workspace role,” “skill group,” and “access policy.”

## Operational considerations

- Every create, rename, archive, restore, and association change should be attributable.
- Bulk changes need bounded request sizes, idempotency, and clear partial-failure handling.
- Group membership counts and filters need pagination at scale.
- Support tooling should make effective membership and, if applicable, effective access explainable.

## Goals

- Workspace-level skill groups.
- Skill-to-group and member-to-group associations.
- Bidirectional inspection and filtering.
- Safe lifecycle and audit behavior.
- Explicit authorization semantics before production rollout.

## Non-goals

- Replacing workspace roles.
- Automatic group inference.
- Cross-workspace or organization-global groups in the initial scope.
- Nested group hierarchies unless separately approved.
- Automatic modification of skill content.

## Acceptance criteria

- Domain groups such as Design, Marketing, Development, and Sales can be represented.
- Authorized administrators can add and remove skills and members idempotently.
- Group, skill, and member views expose consistent associations.
- Search/list operations can filter by group.
- Cross-workspace associations fail safely.
- Archiving a group does not delete skills, members, or audit history.
- Existing ungrouped workspaces continue to work.
- Documentation and UI clearly state whether membership is organizational or access-bearing.

## Assumptions

- A workspace is the tenancy boundary.
- Existing skill and member identifiers remain canonical.
- Existing workspace roles continue to govern who may administer workspace configuration.

## Open questions

- Does group membership grant access, set defaults, or only categorize?
- Can members and skills belong to multiple groups?
- Can admins manage groups, or only owners?
- Are groups available in personal workspaces?
- Are nested groups needed later?
- How should removing a member from a group affect active agent sessions or cached discovery?
- Is bulk assignment required for the first release?`;

const groupArchitecture = `# Architecture & Delivery Plan — ${gIssue}: Support skill groups and workspace member assignments

Backlog issue: [${gIssue}](${gUrl})

## Status

This is a proposed delivery model derived from the request. Exact current schema, API routes, UI components, and authorization helpers were not inspected for this backlog capture and must be verified before implementation.

## Current-state constraints

- Skillplane already has workspace tenancy, members, skills, visibility, authorization, audit, and immutable skill versions.
- Groups must not weaken existing workspace or skill authorization.
- Existing workspaces have no group records and must remain valid.
- Exact role capabilities and current API/MCP extension points are **not yet defined** in this thread.

## Proposed domain model

### skill_groups

Proposed fields:

- stable ID;
- workspace ID;
- name and optional description;
- normalized name for workspace-local uniqueness if uniqueness is desired;
- created/updated timestamps and actor attribution;
- archived timestamp.

### skill_group_skills

Proposed many-to-many association:

- group ID;
- skill ID;
- created timestamp and actor;
- unique constraint on group plus skill.

### skill_group_members

Proposed many-to-many association:

- group ID;
- workspace-member ID;
- created timestamp and actor;
- unique constraint on group plus member.

All associations must enforce the same workspace boundary transactionally. Foreign keys should not cascade-delete canonical skills, users, or historical audit evidence when a group is archived.

## Authorization model

**Required invariant:** existing workspace membership and skill visibility checks run before group behavior.

**Open question:** whether a group is organizational only or grants skill availability.

Recommended sequencing:

1. deliver organizational grouping with no authorization effect;
2. separately specify an explicit access-policy mode and precedence rules if group-based grants are required;
3. add explainability for effective access before enabling enforcement.

Potential administrators are workspace owners and admins, but the exact role matrix must be confirmed against current policy.

## API and MCP surface

**Proposal:** expose deterministic, paginated operations for:

- list/get/create/update/archive/restore groups;
- list group skills and members;
- add/remove skills and members idempotently;
- filter skill/member listings by group;
- optionally bulk-add/remove with bounded batch size and per-item results.

Exact route and tool names are **not yet defined**. Existing caller attribution, optimistic concurrency, idempotency keys, and audit conventions should be reused.

## UI boundaries

- Workspace settings: group lifecycle and membership management.
- Skill catalog: group filters and group badges.
- Skill detail: current groups.
- Member detail: current groups.
- Group detail: paginated skills, members, and recent changes.
- Empty, archived, unauthorized, and partial-bulk states require explicit designs.

## Data flow

1. Authorized actor selects a workspace and group operation.
2. Server resolves actor and workspace membership.
3. Server validates all referenced skill/member records belong to the workspace.
4. Transaction writes the group or association and durable audit event.
5. Read models/search indexes are refreshed or invalidated.
6. API returns canonical state; clients read back the result.

If groups later affect authorization, effective-access caches must be invalidated on every relevant membership or policy change.

## Reliability and concurrency

- Unique constraints prevent duplicate memberships.
- Add/remove operations are idempotent.
- Optimistic concurrency protects metadata edits and archive/restore races.
- Bulk operations use bounded batches and explicit partial results or a transactionally all-or-nothing contract.
- Pagination and stable ordering are required for large groups.
- Archive/restore behavior must be race-safe.

## Security and privacy

- Reject cross-workspace IDs even if the actor can access both workspaces.
- Do not expose private membership information through public skill discovery.
- Preserve least privilege for administration.
- Audit actor, operation, target IDs, source client, and outcome without storing secrets.
- If access-bearing groups are added, deny-by-default precedence and regression tests are required.

## Observability

Track:

- group and membership mutation outcomes;
- authorization denials;
- cross-workspace rejection attempts;
- bulk operation size and partial failures;
- query latency and cardinality;
- effective-access cache invalidation if introduced.

## Migration and compatibility

- Add nullable-independent tables; do not require backfilling existing skills or members.
- Existing queries retain current behavior when no group filter is supplied.
- No default groups should be inferred without an explicit product decision.
- Rollback should disable new surfaces and preserve inert group data for a future retry; avoid destructive down-migrations in production.

## Delivery sequence

### Phase 1: semantics and data contracts

- Decide organizational versus access-bearing behavior.
- Confirm role matrix, uniqueness, multi-group, archive, and personal-workspace rules.
- Define API/MCP contracts and audit events.

### Phase 2: persistence and domain services

- Add schema and constraints.
- Implement workspace-safe lifecycle and association services.
- Add unit, transaction, concurrency, and cross-workspace tests.

### Phase 3: read surfaces

- Add list/detail/filter APIs and indexes.
- Add UI group settings, group detail, and skill/member badges.
- Validate pagination, empty states, and accessibility.

### Phase 4: bulk and operational hardening

- Add bounded bulk workflows if required.
- Add metrics, audit views, failure recovery, and performance tests.

### Phase 5: optional access enforcement

- Only after a separate approved policy specification.
- Add effective-access calculation, explainability, cache invalidation, denial tests, and staged rollout.

## Validation

- Schema and migration tests.
- Domain invariants and duplicate/idempotency tests.
- Role matrix and cross-workspace denial tests.
- API/MCP contract tests.
- UI tests for create/edit/archive/filter and membership flows.
- Audit read-back verification.
- Performance tests for high-cardinality groups.
- Regression tests proving ungrouped workspaces retain current behavior.

## Risks and mitigations

- **Accidental access widening:** keep first release organizational or require explicit deny-by-default policy.
- **Role confusion:** distinguish roles, groups, and policies in UI and docs.
- **Large association sets:** paginate and bound mutations.
- **Stale discovery/access caches:** event-driven invalidation and read-after-write tests.
- **Destructive lifecycle behavior:** archive groups and preserve associations/history.

## Open questions

The product questions in the ideation document are blocking inputs for final architecture, especially access semantics, multiplicity, administrative roles, personal workspaces, and nesting.`;

const sourceIdeation = `# Ideation & Product Rationale — ${sIssue}: Support Git-hosted skill sources and repository-wide imports

Backlog issue: [${sIssue}](${sUrl})

## Context and motivating problem

Skill authors often keep canonical \`SKILL.md\` content in Git. Manually copying that content into Skillplane creates drift, loses source provenance, and turns upstream updates into repetitive publishing work.

The request has two related modes:

1. one managed skill uses one Git-hosted skill file as its source of truth;
2. one repository acts as a shared source for multiple managed skills, with a source view showing every associated skill.

Examples supplied in the discussion:

- Diffpanel file: \`skills/diffpanel-chapters/SKILL.md\` in the Diffpanel repository;
- [vercel-labs/skills](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) as a repository-scale skill collection;
- [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/) as an ecosystem/catalog example.

The exact public Diffpanel repository URL was not supplied; only the repository-relative path is treated as confirmed.

## Target users and stakeholders

- Product teams that publish an official skill alongside their application code.
- Skill collection maintainers managing many skills in one repository.
- Workspace administrators connecting and monitoring external sources.
- Skill consumers who need trustworthy provenance and freshness.
- Security and operations teams responsible for repository credentials, supply-chain risk, sync reliability, and audits.

## Core user journeys

### Connect one official skill file

A Diffpanel maintainer connects a repository, chooses an allowed ref policy and \`skills/diffpanel-chapters/SKILL.md\`, previews the imported content, then creates or links the managed Skillplane skill. Later upstream changes become reviewable Skillplane candidates or versions according to publication policy.

### Import a skill repository

A maintainer registers a collection repository once. Skillplane discovers supported skill roots, previews additions/updates/conflicts, and creates explicit bindings from each managed skill to the common source.

### Inspect source provenance

A user opens a source page and sees all managed skills derived from it, their source paths, resolved commit SHAs, content digests, last sync results, drift, and failures.

### Recover from upstream changes

If a file is renamed, deleted, malformed, or conflicts with another binding, Skillplane reports a non-destructive action state rather than silently deleting or overwriting managed skills.

## Product principles

- Git is the authoring source; Skillplane remains the immutable distribution, authorization, review, audit, and context control plane.
- Every imported version must resolve to an immutable commit, even when tracking a mutable branch.
- Repository content is untrusted input and is never executed during import.
- Sync behavior must be previewable, idempotent, attributable, and recoverable.
- One shared source object should support both single-file and repository-scale modes.
- Existing manually managed skills do not change until explicitly connected.

## Product options and tradeoffs

### Ref strategy

- **Commit pin:** maximally reproducible, but updates require explicit ref changes.
- **Tracked branch/tag:** convenient continuous updates, but every sync must resolve and record a commit.
- **Proposal:** support both, with branch tracking producing immutable commit-backed sync runs.

### Sync trigger

- Manual sync is simplest and easiest to reason about.
- Scheduled polling avoids provider-specific webhook setup but costs API quota.
- Webhooks improve freshness but require installation lifecycle and replay protection.
- **Proposal:** manual first, then configurable webhook or schedule after reliability is proven.

### Repository discovery

- Recursive \`SKILL.md\` discovery is convenient but may be ambiguous in large monorepos.
- A repository manifest is deterministic but adds setup.
- Reusing existing \`skill.json\` metadata may cover some repositories.
- **Open question:** define a precedence order and preview before creating bindings.

### Update policy

- Auto-publish is fast but inappropriate for untrusted or broad changes.
- Existing Skillplane amendment/review policy can decide whether a changed source becomes a candidate or publication.
- **Proposal:** source sync feeds the existing policy instead of creating a parallel publishing path.

## Desired outcomes and success measures

- Teams can connect official Git skill files without maintaining duplicate source text.
- Every Skillplane version can show source repository, path, and commit provenance.
- Repository-scale sources expose a complete, filterable list of associated skills.
- No-op synchronization creates no duplicate versions.
- Sync failures are visible and recoverable without data loss.
- Import does not execute code or leak repository credentials.
- Existing publication review and authorization guarantees remain intact.

Candidate quantitative measures include sync success rate, drift duration, no-op rate, mean recovery time, duplicate-version count, and percentage of imported versions with complete provenance.

## UX considerations

- Source creation should validate URL, provider, access, ref, and discovery before saving.
- A preview should separate additions, updates, unchanged skills, removals, renames, and conflicts.
- Source status should distinguish connected, syncing, current, drifted, action required, auth failed, and unreachable.
- Skill detail should show source provenance and whether local edits or overlays are allowed.
- Source detail should group all associated skills and expose per-skill paths/results.
- Removing a source must explain that immutable skill history remains.

## Operational considerations

- Private-repository credentials require explicit scope, rotation, revocation, and redacted audit behavior.
- Provider rate limits, webhook replay, force-pushes, and deleted refs must be observable.
- Bulk sync needs concurrency limits, resumability, and per-skill results.
- Repository transfer or rename should preserve a stable source identity where possible.
- Source health must not be inferred solely from a successful webhook receipt.

## Goals

- Single-file Git source of truth.
- Repository-wide discovery/import for multiple skills.
- Common source grouping and provenance views.
- Deterministic immutable commit resolution.
- Secure, review-policy-aware synchronization.
- Non-destructive drift and failure handling.

## Non-goals

- Arbitrary repository code execution.
- General-purpose Git mirroring.
- Silent deletion when upstream content disappears.
- Assuming one repository layout.
- Replacing immutable Skillplane versions with mutable remote reads.

## Acceptance criteria

- Repository URL, ref policy, and skill path can configure a single binding.
- Each successful sync records commit SHA, path, digest, timestamp, and outcome.
- Repository discovery is deterministic and previewed.
- A source page lists all associated managed skills and statuses.
- Same commit plus content is idempotent.
- Changed content follows existing review/publication policy.
- Rename, deletion, malformed content, and conflicts are explicit and non-destructive.
- Untrusted-content boundaries prevent execution, path escape, oversized bundles, unsupported files, and secret exposure.
- Manual skills remain unchanged until connected.
- Source removal preserves immutable history.

## Assumptions

- Git repositories can be resolved through provider APIs or a constrained fetch layer.
- Current immutable bundle/version and amendment policy remain authoritative.
- A source and its bindings are workspace-scoped.

## Open questions

- Initial Git providers and authentication methods.
- Supported URL forms and self-hosted Git.
- Branch/tag/commit behavior.
- Manual, scheduled, or webhook sync triggers.
- Discovery manifest and directory conventions.
- Rename/deletion confirmation.
- Overlay or local-edit support.
- Repository fork/transfer identity.
- The role of skills.sh: catalog, resolver, import partner, or reference only.`;

const sourceArchitecture = `# Architecture & Delivery Plan — ${sIssue}: Support Git-hosted skill sources and repository-wide imports

Backlog issue: [${sIssue}](${sUrl})

## Status

This is a proposed architecture based on the requested behavior and Skillplane's known immutable-version model. Exact repository services, database schema, provider abstractions, deployment topology, and UI code must be inspected before implementation.

## Current-state constraints

- Skillplane manages immutable skill bundles and published/candidate versions.
- Existing amendment policy controls review or trusted publication.
- Tenancy, visibility, authorization, audit, and contexts must remain authoritative.
- A mutable Git branch cannot replace immutable Skillplane version identity.
- Exact current Git integration capabilities are **not yet defined**.

## Proposed component model

### Git source registry

A workspace-scoped source record representing a repository and connection policy.

Proposed fields:

## Context and motivating problem

Skill authors often keep canonical `SKILL.md` content in Git. Manually copying that content into Skillplane creates drift, loses source provenance, and turns upstream updates into repetitive publishing work.

The request has two related modes:

1. one managed skill uses one Git-hosted skill file as its source of truth;
2. one repository acts as a shared source for multiple managed skills, with a source view showing every associated skill.

Examples supplied in the discussion:

- Diffpanel file: `skills/diffpanel-chapters/SKILL.md` in the Diffpanel repository;
- [vercel-labs/skills](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) as a repository-scale skill collection;
- [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/) as an ecosystem/catalog example.

The exact public Diffpanel repository URL was not supplied; only the repository-relative path is treated as confirmed.

## Target users and stakeholders

- Product teams that publish an official skill alongside their application code.
- Skill collection maintainers managing many skills in one repository.
- Workspace administrators connecting and monitoring external sources.
- Skill consumers who need trustworthy provenance and freshness.
- Security and operations teams responsible for repository credentials, supply-chain risk, sync reliability, and audits.

## Core user journeys

### Connect one official skill file

A Diffpanel maintainer connects a repository, chooses an allowed ref policy and `skills/diffpanel-chapters/SKILL.md`, previews the imported content, then creates or links the managed Skillplane skill. Later upstream changes become reviewable Skillplane candidates or versions according to publication policy.

### Import a skill repository

A maintainer registers a collection repository once. Skillplane discovers supported skill roots, previews additions/updates/conflicts, and creates explicit bindings from each managed skill to the common source.

### Inspect source provenance

A user opens a source page and sees all managed skills derived from it, their source paths, resolved commit SHAs, content digests, last sync results, drift, and failures.

### Recover from upstream changes

If a file is renamed, deleted, malformed, or conflicts with another binding, Skillplane reports a non-destructive action state rather than silently deleting or overwriting managed skills.

## Product principles

- Git is the authoring source; Skillplane remains the immutable distribution, authorization, review, audit, and context control plane.
- Every imported version must resolve to an immutable commit, even when tracking a mutable branch.
- Repository content is untrusted input and is never executed during import.
- Sync behavior must be previewable, idempotent, attributable, and recoverable.
- One shared source object should support both single-file and repository-scale modes.
- Existing manually managed skills do not change until explicitly connected.

## Product options and tradeoffs

### Ref strategy

- **Commit pin:** maximally reproducible, but updates require explicit ref changes.
- **Tracked branch/tag:** convenient continuous updates, but every sync must resolve and record a commit.
- **Proposal:** support both, with branch tracking producing immutable commit-backed sync runs.

### Sync trigger

- Manual sync is simplest and easiest to reason about.
- Scheduled polling avoids provider-specific webhook setup but costs API quota.
- Webhooks improve freshness but require installation lifecycle and replay protection.
- **Proposal:** manual first, then configurable webhook or schedule after reliability is proven.

### Repository discovery

- Recursive `SKILL.md` discovery is convenient but may be ambiguous in large monorepos.
- A repository manifest is deterministic but adds setup.
- Reusing existing `skill.json` metadata may cover some repositories.
- **Open question:** define a precedence order and preview before creating bindings.

### Update policy

- Auto-publish is fast but inappropriate for untrusted or broad changes.
- Existing Skillplane amendment/review policy can decide whether a changed source becomes a candidate or publication.
- **Proposal:** source sync feeds the existing policy instead of creating a parallel publishing path.

## Desired outcomes and success measures

- Teams can connect official Git skill files without maintaining duplicate source text.
- Every Skillplane version can show source repository, path, and commit provenance.
- Repository-scale sources expose a complete, filterable list of associated skills.
- No-op synchronization creates no duplicate versions.
- Sync failures are visible and recoverable without data loss.
- Import does not execute code or leak repository credentials.
- Existing publication review and authorization guarantees remain intact.

Candidate quantitative measures include sync success rate, drift duration, no-op rate, mean recovery time, duplicate-version count, and percentage of imported versions with complete provenance.

## UX considerations

- Source creation should validate URL, provider, access, ref, and discovery before saving.
- A preview should separate additions, updates, unchanged skills, removals, renames, and conflicts.
- Source status should distinguish connected, syncing, current, drifted, action required, auth failed, and unreachable.
- Skill detail should show source provenance and whether local edits or overlays are allowed.
- Source detail should group all associated skills and expose per-skill paths/results.
- Removing a source must explain that immutable skill history remains.

## Operational considerations

- Private-repository credentials require explicit scope, rotation, revocation, and redacted audit behavior.
- Provider rate limits, webhook replay, force-pushes, and deleted refs must be observable.
- Bulk sync needs concurrency limits, resumability, and per-skill results.
- Repository transfer or rename should preserve a stable source identity where possible.
- Source health must not be inferred solely from a successful webhook receipt.

- Single-file Git source of truth.
- Repository-wide discovery/import for multiple skills.
- Common source grouping and provenance views.
- Deterministic immutable commit resolution.
- Secure, review-policy-aware synchronization.
- Non-destructive drift and failure handling.

- Arbitrary repository code execution.
- General-purpose Git mirroring.
- Silent deletion when upstream content disappears.
- Assuming one repository layout.
- Replacing immutable Skillplane versions with mutable remote reads.

- Git repositories can be resolved through provider APIs or a constrained fetch layer.
- Current immutable bundle/version and amendment policy remain authoritative.
- A source and its bindings are workspace-scoped.

- [Architecture & Delivery Plan](https://linear.app/21n/document/architecture-and-delivery-plan-ski-12-support-git-hosted-skill-sources-20057351abbe)"}]},"readOnlyHint":false,"status":"completed","result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{"id":"SKI-12","title":"Support Git-hosted skill sources and repository-wide imports","description":"## Executive summary\n\nAllow a Skillplane-managed skill to use a Git-hosted skill file as its source of truth, and allow one Git repository to act as a shared source for multiple skills. Expose source-level grouping so users can see every managed skill derived from a given repository or source configuration.\n\n## Problem or opportunity\n\nSkill authors already maintain canonical skill instructions in Git repositories. Copying those files into Skillplane creates drift, obscures provenance, and makes updates manual. Repository-scale collections such as [vercel-labs/skills](<https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills>) and catalogs surfaced through [skills.sh](<https://skills.sh/>) also need a single import and synchronization model rather than one disconnected setup per skill.\n\nA concrete single-skill example is Diffpanel's repository file at `skills/diffpanel-chapters/SKILL.md`.\n\n## Expected outcome\n\nA workspace can register a Git source once, map one file to one managed skill or discover multiple skills from a repository, synchronize immutable Skillplane versions from exact Git revisions, and inspect all skills grouped by their common source.\n\n## Goals\n\n* Represent a Git source with repository identity, provider, ref policy, credentials where needed, and provenance.\n* Configure an individual managed skill from one Git-hosted `SKILL.md` path.\n* Import or synchronize multiple skills from a repository containing a skill collection.\n* Track each published Skillplane version back to an exact commit and source path.\n* Show and filter all skills associated with the same source.\n* Detect changes, additions, removals, renames, failures, and drift without silently overwriting managed state.\n* Support public repositories first while preserving a secure path for private repositories.\n\n## Non-goals\n\n* Executing arbitrary repository code during import.\n* Treating a mutable branch name alone as immutable provenance.\n* Automatically deleting managed skills when upstream files disappear.\n* General-purpose Git hosting or repository mirroring.\n* Assuming every repository follows one directory layout.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n* A user can configure a single source using repository URL, ref policy, and `SKILL.md` path.\n* A successful synchronization records the resolved commit SHA, source path, content digest, timestamp, and outcome.\n* Repository-wide import discovers supported skills deterministically and previews changes before applying them.\n* One source detail view lists every managed skill sourced from it, including sync and drift status.\n* Repeated synchronization of the same commit and content is idempotent and does not create duplicate versions.\n* Changed content creates a reviewable candidate or published version according to the skill's existing publication policy.\n* Missing, renamed, malformed, or conflicting source files produce explicit non-destructive states.\n* Repository content is treated as untrusted input: path traversal, symlink escape, oversized bundles, unsupported files, and secret exposure are prevented.\n* Existing manually managed skills remain unchanged until explicitly connected to a source.\n* Source removal does not erase immutable Skillplane version history.\n\n## Dependencies and risks\n\n* Existing immutable bundle/version, amendment review, visibility, tenancy, audit, and credential models.\n* Git provider API limits, webhook reliability, force-pushes, deleted refs, and private repository authorization.\n* Repository discovery conventions and conflicts between source metadata and Skillplane metadata.\n* Supply-chain risks from compromised repositories or mutable refs.\n* Scale limits for large monorepos and bulk synchronization.\n\n## Open questions\n\n* Which providers and URL forms are supported first?\n* Are refs pinned to commits, tracked branches/tags, or both?\n* Is synchronization manual, scheduled, webhook-driven, or configurable?\n* What repository layouts and manifests define multiple skills?\n* How are upstream rename and deletion intents confirmed?\n* Can one managed skill combine Git-sourced files with Skillplane-managed overlays?\n* How are forks and repository transfers represented without losing provenance?\n* Should [skills.sh](<http://skills.sh>) be integrated as a catalog/discovery layer, a Git source resolver, or both?\n\n## Supporting documents\n\n* [Ideation & Product Rationale](<https://linear.app/21n/document/ideation-and-product-rationale-ski-12-support-git-hosted-skill-sources-25abc9c35487>)\n* [Architecture & Delivery
